text:
Alex Kim: Quick q — customer reported a mismatch: console rollout says 10% to new-model, feature-flag service returns users in experiment A. Which one should win? we had two conflicting configs and traffic went to the flag result.
Mira Santos: Short answer: today it's ambiguous and depends on evaluation order. Long answer: that's bad. We should define a single authoritative source or a clear precedence.
Jordan Lee: We ran into this last quarter. The runtime merges multiple inputs: guard checks, console rollouts, and feature flags. But the merge logic is sprinkled across three services.
Pat O'Neill: Proposal: canonical precedence table stored in rollout-service. ex: 1) Safety guards 2) Console rollout (enterprise overrides) 3) Feature flags (team-level toggles) 4) Local runtime overrides
Alex Kim: That ordering sounds reasonable, but customer expectations differed. They expect feature-flag toggles to flip immediate experiments even if a console canary exists.
Mira Santos: Right — customers see flags as "feature switches" and console as "deployment routing". We need to surface that distinction in the UI and in the API.
Jordan Lee: UX idea: show "effective decision" + provenance chain. e.g. "User routed to new-model (decided by console rollout 10%) — overridden by feature flag 'exp-a'". Should be easy to log.
Pat O'Neill: API-level suggestion: add header `X-Rollout-Decision-Source: console|flag|guard|runtime` on responses and a trace id. Also persist the source in the decision events so telemetry can attribute.
Alex Kim: Perfect. If we add that, ops can query traces to see which source applied. We need metrics: counts by source, and latency impact.
Mira Santos: Also requires a small contract change: rollout-service must accept configured precedence per org (enterprise customers might want their console to always win). So allow an org-level override flag `precedence_policy`.
Jordan Lee: Implementation note: prefer not to hardcode precedence in many places. One config entry in rollout-service that every evaluation reads is better than ad-hoc overrides in feature-flag service.
Pat O'Neill: I'll draft the precedence matrix and a minimal API change. Example payload suggestion:

```
POST /v1/eval
{
  "user_id": "u123",
  "context": {"region":"us-west"},
  "precedence_hint": "console-first"  // optional
}
```

The runtime returns `decision` and `source`.
DeployBot: deploy finished: rollout-service v2.3.0 — feature/precedence-mvp merged by @pat
Alex Kim: Nice, can we also add a console affordance: when creating a rollout, choose its "authority level" (default: normal, can be set to enterprise-override). UI shows a badge.
Mira Santos: Yes — and console should write the authority into the rollout object so the runtime can evaluate deterministically.
Jordan Lee: For backwards compat: if no authority set, fall back to org precedence policy. Keep the header `X-Rollout-Decision-Source` even for older clients.
Pat O'Neill: I'll spin up a tiny RFC and assign JIRA: PLAT-1892. I'll include telemetry fields: decision_source, decision_chain (list), and precedence_used.
Alex Kim: Thanks — main ask from me: make the telemetry queryable and add a dashboard widget for "decision_source by route" so SREs can spot flip-flops quickly.
Mira Santos: I'll take the dashboard mock and wire to the metrics team. :+1:
Jordan Lee: cc @security — ensure no sensitive data in decision_chain logs.
Alex Kim: Good call. Keep IDs only, no PII.
Pat O'Neill: ok PR incoming, will post link in this thread when ready.
Alex Kim: thanks all :rocket:
